A fire-breathing dragon. Tacky, but rich kids love stuff like this.
A classic with an imprint. I could use it as currency if I wanted to.
Red and flashy. Losing it is easy, but finding a new owner for it is a piece of cake too.
The case is nice, but the fence would know it's a cheapo.
Just a lighter. There's one like this in every pocket.
Are you sure you want to leave the clan?
A pile of oily metal. Weighs a ton but is worth very little.
Some people like decorating their car interior with plushies like this. Who am I to judge?
A funny-looking figurine. I'm sure I can find someone who'd want to put it on their dash.
Just a trinket, but car enthusiasts have their own opinions on things like this.
It's a small thing, but nice scents are always in demand.
It smells better than most cars I've been in.
A common car accessory. It doesn't cost much, but it does have character.
A high-quality car stereo. People are willing to pay for good sound.
A pretty good car stereo. A popular model like this is always in demand.
Just a regular car stereo. I'm sure there's someone out there who could use one.
Pricey. People don't buy these if they're trying to save money
Looks pretty good. Could get a decent amount of money for one like this.
A simple dashcam. It's not the best, but it's definitely worth the money.
I often see cars of this brand in the city, but none have this emblem.
A heavy piece of metal. Can lift a car, but I prefer to use car lifts.
Gets rid of hinge squeak. I should sell it to someone who repairs doors after I break them.
Hopefully, the airbag is intact. The thing wasn't easy to remove, but the demand for those is insane.
They might seem small, but you won't get very far without them. It certainly can't hurt to have a spare one.
A well-built air compressor. A useful thing all around. Won't be hard to find a buyer for it.
An expensive model. People usually buy one of those just once, and it lasts a long time.
A bedroom toy. The fur is soft, the metal is sturdy. Don't ask me where I got these.
A weird-looking thing. Seems dangerous. Maybe it's for torture, or maybe for something else.
Keep the barrel well-oiled, or it'll jam at the worst possible moment. That's the law of the streets.
My gun can do without it, and a sealed can is easily turned into cash.
Top-grade composition. It'd be a crying shame to waste on my own gun. Better sell it to some artisan for a hefty sum.
Shines brightly, but the battery is almost dead. Better sell it before it goes out for good.
A toy for professional gunsmiths. I have no use for measuring bullet velocity, but the fence will pay generously for it.
An encrypted remote control for an elite drone. Useless without the drone itself, but someone will pay a fortune for it.
Pins and springs. Small parts that are always getting lost.
You can tell right away that it's handmade. A knife like this is valued for more than just its sharpness.
It's not just a weapon, but a piece of art. I'll hit the jackpot if I don't ruin the packaging.
Has a carbon blade. Looks like a prop from a sci-fi movie.
Nothing but the essentials. Easy to hide in a boot. A valuable item for sale.
Titanium and swag. Too clean for my work, better to sell it.
D2 steel. Cuts perfectly. So beautiful I don't even want to use it.
Gets damp if you look at it wrong and fouls the barrel. Cheap gunpowder for those who couldn't care less if their gun misfires or not.
Makes for a smooth shot with no surprises. Gunsmiths always pay well for it.
A chemical wonder in its purest form. Better sell it for a huge score before it gets me into trouble.
Professional chemicals and brushes. If I break the seal, it will lose its value. Better sell it as is.
A whole suitcase full of tools. For those who love their gun more than their mother.
A cleaning rod and some gun grease. Cleaning the barrel is tedious, but life is more important than being lazy.
Food wrapped in plastic. Tastes like cardboard but doesn't spoil for years.
Too difficult for me to handle. But all these microchips must make it worth the price.
Beautiful watches never go out of style. Especially ones like this.
Looks like military equipment. Things like that are rarely cheap.
With something like this, you definitely won't get lost. And I'm sure there'll be a buyer for it.
I have no idea what it's for. But it looks too expensive to be useless.
I don't want to know what this thing is capable of. The main thing is that it costs an arm and a leg.
A custom piece. If I break one part, I'll lose a fortune. Needs to be sold to a connoisseur, and fast.
Perfect build. Too expensive for dirty work, but can be sold at an excellent price.
Reliable steel. I've got enough tools already, but some extra cash wouldn't hurt. Sell it.
Solid lenses. My future isn't bright enough to warrant these, but mercenaries consistently pay good money for them.
Elite tactical optics. Useless in combat, but fences will gladly transform this into cash.
Armor for man's best friend. Even dogs need protection in Looty Bay.
Has a heavy metal body. Too bad the batteries are dead.
Measures distance with a laser. I won't even bother figuring out how to use it and just sell it.
Fine flame adjustment. Clog the delicate nozzle and you'll lose a ton of money. Better sell it to the experts right away.
Steady flame. I've warmed up my food already, and this thing is easy to turn into quick cash.
It hisses and smokes half of the time. A heavy piece of junk that will bring me some loose change at best.

A loser's deck. Better keep your hand on your holster if you see it on the table.

The card back serves as a distraction. While someone is busy examining the patterns, you're picking their pockets.
Slick cards. Perfect for dealing yourself an ace from your sleeve.
Can be cashed out at <color=#{:palette(Target)}>Lenny's Motel</color>.
Rose gold. Looks flashy. Weighs a lot, though. Fences love this sort of thing.
You can't just buy a watch like this, they are passed down through generations... or stolen from someone too careless.
An expensive skeleton watch. All the gears are visible. It's mesmerizing to watch them spin.
Made of some curious alloy. Lightweight, feels kind of strange. Lovers of the exotic will appreciate it.
A steel brick for your wrist. If the watch breaks, you can use it as a blunt weapon.
Simple strap, reliable mechanism. Swiss precision for those who value their time.
A simple silver ring with a green stone. Subtle yet easily turned into cash.
Vintage gold. They look like something your grandmother would leave you as an inheritance. Weigh quite a bit too.
Bends in half. Gimmicky technology for the sake of flexing. The screen will crack if you look at it wrong.
A real workhorse. The battery holds a charge for so long, it'll probably wait for me to get out of jail.
Every other person has a phone like this. A stolen one would be dirt cheap.
A trendy brick phone for so-called creatives. The camera's good, but the battery's a piece of junk.
The diamonds are dazzling. I could buy half the city with a necklace like this.
A blue noose. It has so many sapphires it will weigh down your neck.
The stones are actually very small, but if you don't look too closely, it will pass for a treasure.
A niche item, but it will quickly find its buyer.
Has a Greek ornament on it. Heavy. Looks like a museum piece. Hope it's not costume jewelry.
A silver thread with pearls on it. Fragile. The pearls scratch easily, so handle with care.
Has a stylish case. Looks powerful and fast. Hope the data can be erased quickly too.
Glows like a Christmas tree. Powerful, heavy, expensive.
Heavy, armored, encrypted. Can be sold, but not hacked.
Can't tell whether it's a tablet or a laptop. A weird hybrid, but the screen looks nice.
A tablet that desperately wants to be a laptop. A fragile toy for office clerks.
Thin and lightweight. The most popular laptop in coffee shops. Will be easy to sell.
A boring ring. It's the kind you usually take off during a divorce proceeding or a robbery.
You don't see a ring like this every day. It's hard to even imagine how much people will pay for it.
The stone shimmers with a pink hue like expensive champagne. It costs so much that I'm afraid to hold it in my hands.
An animalistic grin made of gold. For those who want to appear dangerous.
A chain for your finger. Looks strange, but it's golden and weighs quite a bit.
A massive ring. Could knock someone's teeth out with it. The stone looks expensive.
Vintage gold. They look like something your grandmother would leave you as an inheritance. Weigh quite a bit too.
Two white sparks at the tips. Not crown jewels, but worth a pretty penny.
Look like hairpins, but they're, in fact, platinum. The white stones are cold to the touch.
Exquisite craftsmanship. The design makes them expensive to buy at the store, but I will have to sell them by scrap weight. What a shame.
Sharp angles and geometry. Fashionable, and most importantly, the gold is of good quality.
These stones are worth more than my life. Let's hope I'll make it to the fence alive.
Sees everything. Perfect for filming your arrest in 4K.
A regular point-and-shoot. Made of cheap plastic, but it'll do for blackmailing.
Takes worse pictures than an old phone. It's only good as a beer coaster.
Looks like a construction block, but you won't be able to build a house with it. It will, however, blow the roof of your mind off.
Candy for those who really want to go breaking bad.
Makes criminal life a little sweeter.
Brewed at a temperature of 420 degrees Fahrenheit.
Strong, expensive stuff. Apparently, not for baking.
Restores the integrity of body armor.
Made in collaboration with a fashion designer. He just slapped his name on it, and the price skyrocketed.
A kid in a cap. Limited edition. Geeks would kill for this plastic toy.
A black-and-white, "noir" version of a toy figure. Looks depressing, costs a lot.
The red series. Differs from the basic version only in plastic color and the inflated price.
It stood on the shelf and watched me rob the apartment. Now it's going to gawk at the fence.
Just junk to me, but a fortune to a collector.
You can buy a used car for the same price as this piece of cardboard.
I remember the scandal involving this guy. A dirty reputation always raises the price.
A perfectly average player. Nothing special, but the fans will buy it anyway.
The rookie of the season. Worth mere pennies for now, but who knows?
The Holy Grail. Don't breathe on it and don't bend the corners. This is my retirement plan right here.
A fake antique. It's buried underground for a week to be foisted on experts.
A cheap copy for tourists. The only scary thing about it is its poor quality.
The face is ugly, but it's got some nice embellishments. Antique collectors would kill for this.
Looks like art, burns like firewood. I won't get much money for it.
Heavy, tasteless, and made entirely of gold. My favorite cat breed.
Looks quite friendly. I hope it'll bring me luck in the form of cash.
They used to put mercury in these.
Helps to tell borax from a top-grade product.
Prick your finger and check your blood sugar. Simple as.
Painfully squeezes the arm. Reminds me of how I got cuffed by the cops last month.
Optics for dentists. Or for watching store security.
Some kind of medical device. It probably isn't cheap if it looks so professional.
Cheap condoms. Use at your own risk.
All stuff and no fluff. Protection for a matter of minutes.
In and out. For those who are always in a rush.
As thin as my wallet after an encounter with a police officer. Can barely feel them.
The best you can buy. Or steal.
Banned in half of all countries. A rare but dangerous find.
A murky goop. Could be medicine, could be poison. Not going to test it on myself.
Liquid immunity. People will kill for this vial if an epidemic breaks out.
A medicine for the wealthy. It will save your life if you have money.
Watered-down syrup. Looks like colored tap water.
At your base, you can launder money, open cargo, stock up, and just catch your breath.
A central attraction for criminals from all over the state.
Someone else's base. With the right skills, it can be robbed.

A purple stone. I could use it, but I'd rather sell it.
Icy blue. Not as expensive as a diamond, but costs enough to last a lifetime.
A blood-red stone. Looks sinister, but the price is nice.
Green like dollars. My favorite color.
When I look at it, I don't see the refraction of light, but my comfortable life on a tropical island.

New generation. It's a scarce item, which is why gamers would sell their souls to the devil for it.
Has a stylish white case. It glows too brightly in the dark, though, which is bad news for a thief.

Represents physical strength, unyielding will, and commitment to see things through to the end. Signifies that the person wearing it stood strong in prison and didn't break. Tattooed on those who do not shy away from a fight.
A mockery of the law and a symbol for those who play by their own rules. Represents a cynical worldview and the credo: Seize the day and take any risk with a smirk.
An open admission of a life beyond the pale. Represents an unwavering commitment to the criminal path. A mark for those who refuse to cooperate with the authorities.

An eagle in mid-dive represents resolve and a readiness to strike. It is worn by those capable of moving from words to action without hesitation. A second eagle completes the look and emphasizes the wearer’s character.

Silent grief for freedom. A mark for those who have served long sentences and kept their backbone intact. The choice of those who have embraced their dark side and know the true price of a life outside the system.
A hot temper and a short fuse, ready to explode with anger at any moment. The wearer of this tattoo isn't afraid of conflict and will burn everything in their path to achieve their goal.
A mark of pride, independence, and a spirit so free it cannot be locked away. Side by side, these two birds represent raw strength and undisputed status.
Trust must be earned. This tattoo belongs to the wary and the cold-blooded. Having walked a long road, they know the true weight of words.
Complete control over feelings and emotions. High professionalism. This ink is for those who are not afraid of pain.
If there's no risk, there's no glory. Symbolizes a willingness to go all-in, even under the threat of death. Usually worn by criminals who have committed daring robberies or prison breaks.
One life, one chance. A symbol of a criminal who no longer fears death and has irrevocably accepted their path. Worn by those who've chosen their ultimate path.
Victory against all odds. Living in defiance of circumstance. Worn by those who have been through hell and came out the other side with their prize.
A threat behind a merry mask. A hint of cruelty and unpredictability. Reveals a beastly nature that does not forgive weakness.

A symbol of the bold heist, especially targeting financial institutions. It speaks of high stakes and even higher risks. Typically worn by those who have taken part in armed robberies, armored car heists, or bank raids.
A life lived behind barbed wire. The mark of the system’s brutality and the limits it imposes. Belongs to those who crossed the threshold long ago and spent many years of their lives in a cell.

A total acceptance and understanding of death’s nature. Death is always close, there is no reason to fear her. Inked by those who do not cling to life and are ready to put it all on the line if the stakes are high enough.
A symbol of belonging to the gang's leadership. Worn only by respected and influential criminals who handle serious business.
Represents the "old school" prestige and marks of a criminal underworld veteran. It is the signature of high-status figures and career criminals, forged by years within the system.

Represents an unshakable strength of character. An inner backbone and integrity held before one’s own. Worn by those who never cracked, never snitched, those who endured interrogations and torture but remained loyal to the end.

Every prisoner’s dream. This ink can be a stroke of irony or a sincere drive to break free. Worn by those who refuse to accept their sentence and have not lost hope for liberation. Sometimes inked right before an escape.

Life is one big bet. This ink is a reflection of the philosophy of risk and the roll of the dice. Worn by the high-rollers, the grifters, the cardsharps, and the thieves. Often the signature of gamblers and con artists.
Cash is king. The eye represents total oversight, the power to watch and control. Inked on those who hold the communal pot or deal with large amounts of black-market money.
Represents the readiness to defend one’s interests through force. Worn by those convicted of armed offenses, clashes with the police, and violent settling of scores.

Symbolizes hope for forgiveness and repentance. However, in the criminal underworld, it is often used as pure sarcasm. This tattoo is chosen either by those who truly seek penance, or by those who mock the system by feigning humility they do not feel.

You look like someone fresh out of the joint. No offense. I say that to everyone. Looking for something? Or someone? Ask away, the info's free. But if you need some cash laundered, that's gonna cost you.
Not the talkative type, huh? Well, that's even better. No reason to waste breath. Take a look around. Ask away if you need anything.
I see your type in here every day. You all refuse good ol' advice at first, but then come back with questions. So let's just get straight to the questions.

You'll have to get your hands dirty first. The easiest way is to steal valuable stuff in <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Looty Bay</color> and then sell it. When you get your own land plot, you'll also get more opportunities, like <color=#{:palette(Main)}>cargo</color>. Or a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>farm</color>, if you prefer growing money trees - if you know what I mean.

You will need special workbenches to handle cargo. For storage, use racks. However, it's entirely your call what to do with your cargo: you can <color=#{:palette(Main)}>open</color>, <color=#{:palette(Main)}>repack</color>, <color=#{:palette(Main)}>build a collection</color> out of it. The world is your oyster.

Hit the nail on the head. You can set up processing gear right on your plot - stuff like <color=#{:palette(Main)}>grow rooms</color> or <color=#{:palette(Main)}>chemical laboratories</color>. Feed in the right cargo, give it some time, and out comes top-shelf product. Step one, though: <color=#{:palette(Main)}>get yourself a plot</color>.
To open cargo <color=#{:palette(Main)}>at home</color>, you'll need a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Cargo Workbench</color>. Put the cargo on it and watch it do all the dirty work. You can also modify it.

Yeah, you'll need a separate <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Contraband Workbench</color>. Place it <color=#{:palette(Main)}>in your house</color>, load it with contraband, and watch it... you got the gist. The contraband turns into (almost) legal and (very) in-demand goods.

A collection is a set of valuables put in a single big-ticket cargo. You pack it at the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Collection Table</color>. The better equipped the table, the more options you get. Even thieves have rules and systems, you know.

Order everything you need off the Black Market - feel free to use my laptop for now. When you get <color=#{:palette(Main)}>your own plot</color> and unlock new <color=#{:palette(Main)}>shipments</color>, the catalog gets way better. Plus, hitting a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>higher-level district</color> unlocks the really good stuff.

I thought you liked working together. But seriously though, buy a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>house</color> to launder at home. Upgrade the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Laundering Desk</color> to launder more. It's that simple.

Find an owned <color=#{:palette(Main)}>settlement</color> to rent yourself a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>plot</color>. You can pay cash for your first spot, but stepping up to higher-level districts takes official papers. There'll ba a trailer for you already - and there it is, your first home. If you've got the cash and the nerve, hell, you can buy out the whole <color=#{:palette(Main)}>settlement</color>.

Districts across the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>global map</color> are broken down into <color=#{:palette(Main)}>three levels</color>. Set up your plot in a higher-level district, and you'll unlock top-tier shipments and Black Market gear. Just remember, prime spots don't stay empty - expect heavy competition.

New shipments unlock on the Black Market. Most take straight cash, but some call for larger jail time. The top-tier shipments are strictly reserved for <color=#{:palette(Main)}>top-level districts</color>.

And where are you going to store your <color=#{:palette(Main)}>cargo</color> and items? Go on, get yourself a land plot, <color=#{:palette(Main)}>furnish it</color>, and you can finally buy yourself <color=#{:palette(Main)}>a ride</color>. It's all legit. Well, almost. See? So it's not just a waste of money.
Set up racks and item storages to stash your loot. And don't forget about security. Workbenches, tables, and desks are your main tools. With them, believe me, things will get cozier.

Look, <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Looty Bay</color> is a magnet for all sorts of people, but right now we're in my <color=#{:palette(Main)}>motel</color>. You can even see the Prison from here. Pay special attention to the districts, though. They're divided into <color=#{:palette(Main)}>levels</color>, and each has its own <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Sales Center</color> and lots of <color=#{:palette(Main)}>settlements</color>. Got it?

That's... a residential area, basically a wasteland. There are land plots there for your house or whatever you wanna build... <color=#{:palette(Main)}>You rent a plot</color>, and when you launder cash or buy something via your laptop, you pay a percentage to the owner. You can become an owner yourself, if you're up for it.

Those are places where you can sell everything that's weighing down your trunk. The payout depends on the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>district level</color>. Everyone can enter, but only those who rent a plot there have access to the Sales Center.

Looty Bay is where all the action is. There you can open a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>bank account</color> and find fences, smugglers, and all sorts of shady traders. The main thing is to decide who you are. A random <color=#{:palette(Main)}>civilian</color>? Maybe a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>criminal</color>, hiding your face behind a mask? Or <color=#{:palette(Main)}>a cop</color>... All the roles have their pros and cons, except for being a cop. That's just cons.

You can rent plots in <color=#{:palette(Main)}>settlements</color> that have owners. Find a rental sign, "make" a deal, admire your house, plant a tree. Most importantly, put a good fence around everything, so nobody can stick their nose in your business.

Then the Sales Center isn't an option for you. You'll have to visit the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>city</color>. But remember, Looty Bay plays by its own rules. Once you're in the city, take care of the product as soon as possible, or it'll be taken care of for you.

Sure. Put a mask on, and Looty Bay will turn into a battlefield. TThe downside is that everyone sees you as an enemy, and when you're offed, they take everything. The upside is that you can grab <color=#{:palette(Main)}>items and cargo</color> guilt-free. <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Sell</color> your items right away, or <color=#{:palette(Main)}>start a collection</color>.

Listen, I don't want anything to do with cops, not even fake ones. All I know is the Police Department is short-staffed. Go to the city, talk to an <color=#{:palette(Main)}>officer</color> at the precinct. Well, if you're really into all that cop fantasy: chases, shootouts, and donuts.

That's a weird question. They just live. Keep a low profile. Often it's a temporary stage, to get the lay of the land. To scout a spot for future operations... Blend in with the crowd and learn the area. No one will lay a finger on you, let alone touch your stuff.
It's simple: either at the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Sales Center</color> in your district, or somewhere in the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>city</color>. Depends on the circumstances.

You can <color=#{:palette(Main)}>rent</color> one to start things off, but once you buy a house, get something serious with a spacious trunk to stuff more cargo and items in. By the way, a car you buy won't disappear if you die. Remember that.

Well, to upgrade it, you have to buy it first. Once you have the keys and decide to upgrade it, my advice would be to start with the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>trunk</color>. And don't forget the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>hood</color> and the <color=#{:palette(Main)}>underbody</color>. By the way, if you die, the mods on your car won't disappear.
If you don't own a car, then you have to rent one using any Parking Terminal. The thing is, you can't upgrade a rental. It's always in the terms of the agreement. In fine print, of course.

It's important to understand that without <color=#{:palette(Main)}>your own house</color>, you can't use any cars. Rentals only. But that's not all. If you want a cooler ride, you'll have to move to a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>higher-level district</color>. That's how it is.

Our job is to protect this city. <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Arrest Criminals</color> and <color=#{:palette(Main)}>confiscate their bags</color> to earn a paycheck. End of shift, grab your <color=#{:palette(Main)}>cut from me</color>. We'll <color=#{:palette(Main)}>hold onto your personal gear and hand it back</color> when you clock out. Uniforms and weapons are department-issued, but you're only getting the bare basics.

You need <color=#{:palette(Main)}>badges</color> for that. Badges are your ticket to better gear. The rarer the badge, the better the gear. Badges are <color=#{:palette(Main)}>single-use</color>. You can find them <color=#{:palette(Main)}>all over the city</color>. This is not a call to action!

<color=#{:palette(Main)}>Arrest robbers</color>, <color=#{:palette(Main)}>confiscate their belongings</color>, and uphold the law. The better the gear you confiscate, the more you get paid. At the end of the shift, your salary is paid out with what's in the warehouse. <color=#{:palette(Main)}>Only a small part of it is in cash</color>. Such are the times!

There are a couple of ways. First, use the Surrender Order. It will temporarily increase your payout for a successful arrest. Second, patrol with an Active Siren. That also grants a temporary bonus to your salary. Enlist by answering a <color=#{:palette(Main)}>call for backup</color>, and you'll score temporary hazard pay on top of your paycheck.

<color=#{:palette(Main)}>Arresting</color> means slapping handcuffs on a Criminal. They must surrender or be <color=#{:palette(Main)}>knocked out</color> first. Next comes <color=#{:palette(Main)}>imprisonment</color>: after a short delay, the detainee will be imprisonned automatically, but you can speed up the process yourself. Once they are imprisonned, you can collect your reward.
How to earn more money for service?

Set up a <color=#{:palette(Second)}>Grow Room</color> to grow rare types of plants. Once the growth cycle is complete, the product can be sold to the <color=#{:palette(Second)}>Fence</color>. Upgraded equipment will speed up plant growth.
So, the vault was broken into just five times last week. One of those times even the cops showed up. Oh, didn't see you here. Are you here on business?
Hello. Step up to the glass, please. Just keep your hands where I can see them. The guards have a long list of reasons to be nervous.
I'll be right with you. Just let me finish this report before the numbers change again.
The vault is operating routinely. Access is restricted, and as expected, the interest is high.
And what if it's broken into?
You said "if". That's very polite. People here usually say "when". Everyone will hear the drill, and the cops won't be the first to arrive.

A bank account lets you <color=#{:palette(Main)}>launder dirty cash</color>. Once clean, the funds hit your account - ready to be spent without walking around with suspicious stacks of bills in your pockets.

For <color=#{:palette(Main)}>secure keeping</color>: money in your account cannot be stolen. Credits are also required for <color=#{:palette(Main)}>clan operations</color>. Not everything can be settled with cash - sometimes crime has to become organized.
Is clean money strictly for clan operations?

Nope. You can <color=#{:palette(Main)}>cash them out</color> at an ATM or through me anytime you want. Just keep in mind: once withdrawn, it's cash in your pockets again. Along with all the risks that come with it.
Criminals love B-Coin. It's bought for credits and held like crypto with no need to carry it in your pocket. Even the feds can't touch it during a seizure.
Aren't you afraid to work here?
I am. But I have a mortgage on an apartment in a district where the lights still work at night. That's a stronger leash than any security.
Hello. I'll be right with you, just getting this box out of the way. Wouldn't want anyone to trip.
Tell me right away if you don't feel good. I'm not a doctor, but I'll try my best to help.
Are you here for medicine? Sorry, just asking. A lot of people don't come in for that these days.
What should I get for the base?
First aid kits. Better have a few around. When it all starts, you might not make it to the one you have.

A raid. When you have intruders, time is short. A first aid kit will help you get bandaged, come to your senses... sometimes it even lets you choose where to wake up. That's important when there's no one around but enemies.
Why is it so quiet here?
People buy what they need and promptly leave. No one wants to stand by the window any longer than they have to.
Yes. But if I close down, my customers will buy from those who dilute medicine with water.
I try my best. Even if a person is bad, their pain is real. That might sound stupid, though.
What if I helped a guy carry the goods to their car for cash during a robbery? I'd make a little money, they'd leave faster, the shelves would be cleared... Oh, hi!

I don't get why that batch didn't sell. The labels were perfect, the glue was fresh... I guess people are just too suspicious these days. But the scheme was solid, I'm sure of it. Anyway, what do you want?
Come on in, don't be shy. It's surprisingly quiet today. If you're looking for something specific, ask right away. The stuff on the shelves is just for display.
What do you have for sale?

There's only water, candy bars, and some cheap stuff on display to make the shop look alive. All the valuable stuff is locked up in the back. I've got plenty of solid ideas too, but those I don't sell.
What's the word on the street?

Nothing good. Let me guess what's in your trunk. Nothing, or just some cheap cargo? Contraband, on the other hand, is a different story. But it needs to be "polished up" and packaged. Everyone wants it to look marketable.
Everyone wants a pretty picture. The same junk pays way more if it's in a nice box. Packaging makes the item valuable in the buyer's eyes.
What if I just sell it all as is?

Your call. You'll sell it fast, but for next to nothing. It can be an option if you're in a tight spot. You might regret being too lazy to spend a few minutes getting the goods in proper shape, though.
Why is it so clean if it gets robbed all the time?

Looty Bay is a storefront. If this place gets dirty, people will realize the whole system's falling apart. Clean floors and bright lights create the illusion of order. As long as the shop is sparkling, they let us run our business.
Welcome to... sorry, I forget what today's special is called. You want a burger or something cheaper?
Order number... Oh, you haven't ordered anything yet. Sorry, I'm a little under the weather today.
Hi. Do you want sauce with your order? Oh, wait, you haven't even said why you're here. Sorry, force of habit.
Not really. Everyone gets takeout or orders delivery. It's dangerous to sit inside, especially by the window.
Yeah, all the time. With the constant robberies, no one even notices. Written-off buns, dents in the register... for some reason, it all looks the same on the report.
It's awful. My feet ache, I have to smile, the register might get robbed, and then the manager will ask why I didn't offer the robber a combo meal.
To where? Everywhere pays poorly, they just put you in a different uniform. I'm saving up for a ticket. I'll leave this place forever and never ask "Do you want sauce with that?" again.
Tell me about your weirdest customer.

There was that one guy who called himself Fisherman. But instead of a fishing rod, he carried a bunch of grenades on his belt. He said he fished like that everywhere, even in parking lots. The main thing was to find a tall enough bush. He was really weird.
I almost figured out why this power supply is beeping, even though it's turned off. Oh, a customer. Hello.
Welcome. Just don't touch anything, please. Especially the cheap-looking stuff. It usually breaks easily.
Hello. Please don't place anything on the display case. It was cracked before I even got here, but I'll be the one to get blamed.

I love collecting sets. Cameras, laptops, headphones, smartphones... Sometimes I even get offered hefty sums for my collections, but I always refuse. To me, my collectibles are more valuable than any money.

You bet. The rich love to show them off, it's a status symbol for them. But they don't want to collect themselves, just the finished product. Although, in my opinion, the process itself is the most interesting part.
I prefer to sell everything at once.

You can, but that makes no sense. A camera, a phone, headphones, laptops, a video card, even ones that've been to a crypto farm... they've all got a story. Oh, but sorry, you're probably just asking about the price. It's just cheaper all at once.
Like clockwork. The alarm always alerts the cops, but it doesn't mean they'll actually show up.
Leave the car at the gate. There's not enough room for it here.
Get to the point. If it smokes, pings, or won't drive, you've come to the right place.
I'm listening. But make it quick. I've got a car on the lift.
Can you get by without a car?
You can. Not for long, though. A car carries what doesn't fit in a bag, and gets you away when you can't escape on your own two feet.
It's all about placement. Trunk, hood, underbody. Each has its own modifications. If you mix things up, the mod just won't fit.
It says right there on the label. One module increases capacity, another improves acceleration, and the third one makes driving easier. I'm not going to read it for you.
Is it actually possible to escape the cops?

It's totally possible. Just don't try to outspeed them on straightaways in a basic car - they will catch up. Try shaking them in the turns: force them to brake and steer hard. While they accelerate again, you get a real chance to escape. That's the whole secret. Just make sure you don't crash into the very first pole.
Don't touch anything. The stuff isn't kept loaded, but people still manage.
If you're choosing by color, go to a clothing store. If you have questions that ain't stupid, ask away.
Don't stand in front of the barrel, even an empty one. It's a good habit to avoid such situations. You'll live longer.
What's the difference between different weapon versions?

It's the parts. The standard version has a basic setup. The MK2 and later models are equipped with a holographic sight. ADS speed, weapon spread, and range falloff can also vary. Available upgrades depend on the gun - a bigger number doesn't necessarily mean each bullet hits harder.

Many MK3 variants also have larger magazines. But not all of them - some reload faster, while others boast better base stats. Always check the specific gun. A bigger mag comes in handy when a firefight drags on.
Where do all these guns come from?
Look closely. There aren't many new weapons. Most of them just change hands. The story of a single piece can be richer than yours or mine.
Okay, that's it for the weapons.
Tell me the size right away. I don't eyeball it anymore, because then everyone complains that the armor is too tight to breathe.
Everything's in its place. If there's a stain on an item, it's most likely not by design.
If you're here for protection, take your pick. If you're here for a guarantee, we don't do those.
Where do new shipments come from?
There are many sources. Some armor is skimmed off during border crossings, and some comes from old military depots. I'd rather not dwell on where the rest comes from.
Everything's clean on paper. The rest isn't my problem.
Something you can move in. Heavy armor won't help if you're stuck in it like a fixture. Light armor won't save you if you're the first one through the door.
Because it buys you time. A second, or a few. A second is a lot, if you know what to do with it.

No-no-no, I'm not doing any schemes today. The cash register is over there, the shelves are there, I'm just a guy with a name tag.
I'd love to help, but I've got a bad back, there's a camera, and my memory is terrible. You go ahead, I'll look the other way.
Please, don't come any closer. I'm not hiding anything. Take what you need and leave, okay?
I can't talk when you're looking at me like that. Sorry. I really can't help.
I'm just a cashier. They take away even our tips. Please don't ask me anything.
